{"id":"3a919f75-e9f0-4ecc-a821-12f385e82f0b","uuid":"3a919f75-e9f0-4ecc-a821-12f385e82f0b","name":"kodezart v0.3 — loop orchestration: scopes as input, the tracker as live run state","summary":"The graph's input generalizes from a ticket to a scope (initiative | project | milestone | issue): organize everything fireable, walk the blockedBy topology, run fires as sub-graphs, cross issues off as criteria pass, open several PRs with CI folded in.","description":"## The transformation

kodezart v0.2 ends with a self-running loop over **single fires**: prep → approve → fire → groom, one ticket in, one ralph loop, one PR out. v0.3 generalizes the input: the graph takes an entire **scope** — an initiative, a project, a milestone, or a single issue — and runs the whole delivery loop over it. Step 1 makes everything in scope fireable (organize/spec, even stubs and triage items); step 2 reads the organized scope and handles acceptance criteria per fire; the ralph loop's evaluator records which branch owns which issue and crosses issues off in the tracker as criteria pass; validation pulls from the tracker; the run opens several PRs respecting the dependency topology; and CI/CD stops being its own node because the landing machinery monitors checks itself. **From prompt orchestration to loop orchestration** (founder charter, 2026-08-07).

## The recursion that grounds it

The manual 2026-08-07 spec sweep of the v0.2 board — assess → adversarially verify → write, per lane, against the spec rubric — **is the behavioral spec for the organize step**, exactly the way <issue id="5eee576d-1af6-48ab-ba1f-47587ca52fc2" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-50/adopt-the-scheduled-routine-prompts-fire-prep-grooming-as-the">KOD-50</issue> adopts the routine prompts as behavioral spec for the passes. And the v0.2 initiative's progress-verification protocol — read it there; it is not summarized here, because a summary of a contract is a second version of it — is precisely the contract the scope orchestrator executes mechanically — with one substitution, which the design rulings below own and nothing here paraphrases: Ruling A's trigger for Done (demonstrated in the branch carrying the work). The v0.2 board itself is the reference scope: the A/B for this initiative is a scope run over a board shaped like v0.2's, reproducing what was done by hand.

**Measured against that board, 2026-08-08 — the A/B does not start yet, and the reason is arithmetic.** A phase-3 dry run computed what a walk over the reference board would do today. The board's current ready set is two lanes, each `blockedBy` two *mutually unordered* lanes. `KOD-75` D9d resolves a lane's base to its highest-ordered blocker's branch and requires every other blocker's branch to be an ancestor of it; measured with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` over all six ordered pairs of the three lane branches on origin, **no lane branch is an ancestor of any other** — they are siblings cut from trunk, which is the correct shape for lanes the board declares parallel roots. So both ready lanes raise `UnstackableLaneError` and the walk dispatches nothing. D9e's remedy — a linearizing edge added by organize at stage 1 — is unavailable at that point, because both blockers have already run and pushed divergent branches and no deliverable anywhere rebases a lane branch. Base-resolvability is a property of the topology alone and is therefore computable before any branch exists; `KOD-109` owns moving the check to plan time. Until it lands, the reference-scope A/B is not runnable, and that is a fact about the plan, not about the board.

## The graph, before and after (alignment record, 2026-08-07)

**OLD — v0.2 (after the v0.2 stack lands): one fire = one issue, everything in-fire.** Every fire authors its own inputs — three generation sessions per fire, re-paid on every retry; state lives in-process; `queue:*` labels only; one PR out.

```
INPUT: one issue, queue:approved            ← human act PER ISSUE
  │
  ▼
generate_branch          (mints kodezart/{slug}-{hex})
  ▼
generate_ticket          (authors the spec — a full judgment session)
  ▼
generate_criteria        (authors criteria — a full judgment session)
  ▼
validate_criteria        (KOD-66 gate; dirty → bounded regenerate)
  ▼
persist_artifacts
  ▼
RALPH LOOP               (execute ⇄ evaluate, until accepted/stall)
  ▼
merge → review ⇄ fix → open_pr → monitor_ci → complete
                                  ▲ its own node
```

**NEW — v0.3: the generation work moves OUT of the fire, up into scope stages.** The structural claim at the heart of the design: for staged issues, tickets and criteria are no longer produced inside fires at all — they are produced by the scope stages (or pre-warmed by prep) and consumed frozen by execution-only fires.

```
SCOPE RUN  (input: ScopeRef = initiative | project | milestone | issue,
            admitted by the APPROVAL LABEL — one human act, cascading
            over everything within the labeled hierarchy node)
  resolve_scope
    ─► STAGE 1 · organize: every issue specced fireable; per-issue stage
         label set (e.g. queue:approved:ticket — names via OperationConfig)
         ONLY on an issue that passes the stage's ADMISSION TEST
         BARRIER: advance only when ALL issues in scope carry it
    ─► STAGE 2 · criteria: generated + validated for every issue; stage
         label set (e.g. queue:approved:criteria) on the same condition
         (its admission test being a clean KOD-66 verdict)
         BARRIER: all issues staged
    ─► plan_topology (computed: blockedBy walk → lanes, parallel roots)
    ─► STAGE 3 · scope walker: for each READY lane (concurrency from config)
          fire = per-ticket sub-graph dispatched EXECUTION-ONLY
                 (ticket + criteria pre-staged; generation nodes bypassed;
                  stacked lanes get a per-dispatch criteria re-validation
                  against the resolved base via the KOD-66 gate)
            RULING NODE: every open question ruled ONTO THE TRACKER before
              the loop's first iteration — execution-only means generation
              is never re-paid, not that the inputs are decision-complete
              (a question the run CANNOT answer is written to the tracker
               too, as it is raised — never carried to a later stage)
            ralph loop, with the lane's live run-state record edited at
              commit cadence and lane events posted (ruling below)
            evaluator write-back: issue↔branch recorded; each criterion
            DEMONSTRATED IN THE BRANCH → issue crossed off (Done)
            lane fire DONE when its sub-issues are Done and the lane-level
            Verification is demonstrated in that branch → dependents
            unlock HERE, and stack on this lane's branch, never on a merge
          landing coordinator: consolidate → open PR → watch checks —
            and stop. Merging is a human act outside the loop, so several
            open PRs, parallel or stacked, is the steady state
                                                   (CI folded in;
            no standalone monitor node at either level)
    ─► scope terminal: per-lane outcomes + progress report — it AGGREGATES
         and reports, and is never the first writer of anything

  NOTHING above runs without scope:approved — the label triggers the run.
  Fire prep (heartbeat, separate mandate) grooms and specs not-yet-approved
  material so stage 1 moves fast when approval lands; it runs no stages
  and sets no stage labels.
```

### Where each v0.2 node went

| v0.2 node | v0.3 location |
| -- | -- |
| `generate_ticket` | **Stage 1** — once per issue, breadth-first (often pre-done by prep) |
| `generate_criteria` + validation | **Stage 2** — once per issue, breadth-first (+ cheap re-check at dispatch for stacked lanes only) |
| `generate_branch` | still per fire, but **association lookup first** — reuse the recorded branch, mint only if none |
| ralph loop | **unchanged**, per fire — preceded by the fire-time ruling node; plus the cross-off write-back and the live run-state record |
| merge / review / fix | per fire, feeding the coordinator |
| `open_pr` + `monitor_ci` | **landing coordinator** — CI folded in, `monitor_ci` gone as a node; its terminal act is an open PR with its checks watched, never a merge (Ruling B) |
| `complete` | per-lane outcome → aggregated by the **scope terminal** |
| *(nothing)* | new: barriers, walker, coordinator, terminal, prep pre-warming, audit (L7), the fire-time ruling node, the live per-lane run-state record |

**Degeneration case:** a single issue with no stage labels runs the OLD graph unchanged — the stage labels toggle the generation-node bypass per issue, so today's flow is the base case of the new machine, not a parallel path.

### One concrete run: scope = {A, B, C}, B blockedBy A

```
t0  APPROVAL label set on the project          (human act — the only one;
      cascades to A, B, C and anything later parented under them)
t1  STAGE 1: A, B, C specced      → all queue:approved:ticket
t2  STAGE 2: criteria for A, B, C → all queue:approved:criteria
      (B's criteria referencing A's not-yet-existing code: "pending", fine)
t3  STAGE 3: roots = {A, C} → fire BOTH in parallel
      A: rule → ralph → A's Verification DEMONSTRATED IN A's BRANCH →
         A crossed off (Done) → A's FIRE DONE → PR#1 opened, checks watched
      C: rule → ralph → demonstrated in C's branch → C crossed off →
         C's FIRE DONE → PR#2 opened, checks watched
      (each lane's run-state record goes live at its first push, so both
       are locatable from the tracker long before either PR exists)
t4  A's FIRE BEING DONE unlocks B — PR#1 is still open and nothing waits
      on it → B's criteria re-validated against the base it stacks on,
      which is A's branch → fire B there (on its recorded branch if one
      exists) → PR#3 opened against A's branch, checks watched
t5  TERMINAL: [A ✓, B ✓, C ✓] → progress report on the project; every PR
      the run opened is still open, and that is the expected end state
t6  (later, audit tick): L7 re-verifies each Done claim independently
      against the branch that carries it, and may reopen with evidence
```

**Resumability in one line:** dies at t3½ with A's fire Done, PR#1 open and C mid-loop → re-entry re-reads labels, issue states and open PRs — never merge state, which it never waits on: stages 1–2 skip (labels present), A skips (fire Done), C resumes on its recorded branch — located from C's live run-state record, which exists whether or not C ever reached a PR — and B is already unlocked, because A's fire is Done.

## Design rulings (founder, 2026-08-07/08)

**Simplification discipline — plan amendment, 2026-09-08.** SOLID, DRY and hexagonal boundaries apply through the native facilities of Pydantic, FastAPI and uv, with KISS as the governing constraint: an abstraction must remove an observed invalid state, duplicated invariant or dependency problem. <issue id="a35bb59e-e287-4baa-9ddf-0cc099bfd07c" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744/v03-architecture-simplification-plan-typed-privacy-focused-settings">KOD-744</issue> owns the concrete engineering acceptance and primary-documentation references. [KOD-744](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-744>) carries the accepted architecture work and verification boundaries. Stable constants and provider grammars belong in code at the boundary that owns them; configuration is for demonstrated operator/deployment variation with an actual consumer. A literal-ban test is not a reason to add a setting. Known references and generated tracker aggregates are admitted from typed data before rendering, with adapter-owned parsing and operation-supplied privacy facts; authored and third-party prose still receives the required semantic/privacy checks. Obsolete scanner/configuration prescriptions are forward-superseded by the amended owning criteria, while completed v0.2 evidence stays historical. Simplification has explicit tracked work and must be demonstrated through the composed application before its revised criteria are Done. Dependencies and progress remain issue edges and live queries.

* **Done means demonstrated in the branch (Ruling A — founder, 2026-08-08).** An issue is Done when its Verification section is demonstrated in the branch carrying the work. The order: criteria demonstrated in the branch → sub-issue Done → every sub-issue Done plus the lane-level Verification demonstrated → the lane's fire Done. The reason no later event may be substituted: tracking acceptance criteria and then withholding Done until something else happens makes the criteria pointless, and it is circular — the decision to ship consumes the cross-offs, so it cannot also produce them, and a board that waits drains itself of exactly the signal that decision needs. The audit re-verifies independently, also against the branch, and may reopen with evidence; that pass and its non-substitution invariant are [KOD-79](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-79/v03-l7-audit-pass-grooming-transformed-critically-evaluate-the>)'s. **This section owns the Done trigger for v0.3 runs and states it once.** The v0.2 progress-verification protocol is inherited for everything else it rules — read it there — with Ruling A substituted for its landed-PR trigger: a forward supersession on the v0.3 side, the pattern already used for [KOD-51](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-51/pr-1-adapter-reliability-no-ci-classification-transient-404-tolerance>)'s node placement, and no frozen v0.2 body is edited. Under the precedence ruling below, lane text that still gates Done on a merge is a restatement to delete, not a claim to weigh.
* **kodezart opens pull requests and never merges them (Ruling B — founder, 2026-08-08).** The machine's terminal act for a lane is an OPEN pull request whose checks it watches. Merging is a human act entirely outside the loop — which is why several pull requests open at once, parallel or stacked on one another, is the expected steady state and never a condition to be resolved. **Nothing downstream may be gated on a merge:** a dependent lane unlocks when its blocker's FIRE IS DONE (Ruling A) and stacks on that blocker's branch. The consequences belong to their lanes and are not restated here — the coordinator's terminal act and its check-watching to [KOD-77](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-77/v03-l5-landing-coordinator-multi-pr-landing-with-ci-folded-in-at-both>), the unlock arithmetic and the base a stacked lane resolves against to [KOD-75](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-75/v03-l3-topology-planner-scope-walker-blockedby-graph-execution>), the write-back that makes Done-ness readable to [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>), the vocabulary a run ends in to [KOD-78](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-78/v03-l6-scope-terminal-per-lane-outcome-vector-initiative-progress>). The concept map, the NEW-graph diagram, the node-relocation table and the worked example above were corrected to this ruling on 2026-08-08; each had described a machine that merges its own work.
* **Structure lives in the tracker and is derived, never restated (founder, 2026-08-08).** Two halves of one law, and the second is what keeps the first from being quietly undone.
  * **The blocking graph IS the stack specification.** A lane's base is COMPUTED — from its blockers as the tracker records them, together with each blocker's recorded deliverable ref. The issue↔branch association plus the blocking graph is sufficient: no git-side naming convention, no configuration file and no written-down stack is needed, and none is permitted. **Nothing enumerates a concrete stack anywhere** — not an issue body, not a prompt, not a comment, not a README. A sentence naming which lane stacks on which is a snapshot of a graph the tracker already owns, and it rots the moment an edge changes; state the RULE, and let the graph answer the instance. This is the no-derived-aggregate-on-a-durable-surface ruling recorded below, applied to structure rather than to counts. The consequences are what make it useful rather than merely tidy. A lane with several blockers has a base combining all of them and the tracker says which, so the combination is derived rather than declared — and it must be **deterministic**, or two runs produce different bases from the same graph. Changing the graph changes the stack: add a blocker and the base changes, which makes that lane's recorded base stale and, under F19, lapses every criterion graded on it. Staleness is therefore **detectable without anyone having to notice it** — compare a lane's recorded base against the base its current blockers imply. The arithmetic that does all of this belongs to the lane that owns base resolution, [KOD-75](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-75/v03-l3-topology-planner-scope-walker-blockedby-graph-execution>), and is not specified here. **Constructing a working base is not merging a pull request:** Ruling B forbids the latter as a human's decision about shipping, and no implementer may read a permission to stack as a permission to merge.
  * **A prompt carries configuration and pointers, never tracker state.** Where to look, and what the rules are, belong in a prompt; what is currently there is read at runtime through the port. The reason is sharper than the rule: a prompt that embeds the graph is frozen at authoring time and then copied, so it is a second source of truth with a **shorter half-life than a document** — the failure mode of a restatement, arriving faster. Recorded honestly, because it was learned by making the mistake: the pass that first recorded this very law hardcoded the dependency graph into its own prompt while instructing its agents to derive live state through the tracker. That detail is the argument, not an aside. The rule binds every prompt this system renders, and most directly the tracker-native fire composition's fragment, which renders configuration and must tell a session WHERE TO LOOK rather than what is there; that lane is [KOD-105](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-105/v03-l9-tracker-native-fire-composition-one-node-set-two-compositions>), and its design is not restated here.
* **Organize is judgment; walking is arithmetic.** The organize step is a judgment surface (agent sessions with explicit grants, per the v0.2 session-policy discipline); the topology walk, ready-set computation, and cross-off transitions are computed, never judged — the standing selection ruling applied one level up.
* **CI folding at both levels.** The landing coordinator owns check-watching everywhere: scope-level multi-PR delivery AND the per-fire graph — the standalone `monitor_ci` node dissolves. Recorded as a **forward supersession**: <issue id="c211686e-0f7c-4bdc-a17d-38080247a104" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-51/pr-1-adapter-reliability-no-ci-classification-transient-404-tolerance">KOD-51</issue>/<issue id="aa864b5e-bee1-42b1-864c-bcf6b83a663a" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-42/monitor-ci-refs-with-no-ci-loop-the-full-poll-budget-and-route-into">KOD-42</issue>/<issue id="67e1745e-9e34-4a25-8d02-44aa5437148a" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-9/monitor-ci-poll-loop-crashes-the-workflow-on-transient-404-from">KOD-9</issue> land in v0.2 as specced (the adapter classification logic is consumed here, the node placement is superseded here); no frozen v0.2 body is edited.
* **Port widening is deliberate v0.3 scope.** <issue id="188b3e2c-8b7c-430e-8ec6-27d9a6cf3764" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-57/vendor-neutral-tracker-port-linear-adapter-first-of-n-github-issues">KOD-57</issue>'s exclusion of container concepts stands for v0.2; v0.3 adds scope containers (initiative/project/milestone) to the tracker-port domain vocabulary as its own conformance-tested surface. **Generalized 2026-08-08:** the container vocabulary turns out to be the first instance of a pattern rather than a single exception. What changed is that the widening is now a declared discipline applied to every concept v0.3 adds to the port, with the three-layer statement and the boot-time capability rule owned by the port-widening section below and not restated here.
* **Scopes nest; compatibility by degeneration.** An issue-scoped run degenerates to today's single-fire behavior — the existing behavior is the base case of the new machine, not a parallel path.
* Frozen-fire discipline is inherited unchanged. So is the v0.2 progress-verification protocol, in everything it rules except the trigger for Done, which Ruling A above replaces and which is stated only there.
* **Resumability by reconciliation (founder, 2026-08-07).** A scope run is not a process — it is a property of durable state: the tracker (crossed-off issues, lifecycle states, issue↔branch associations) plus the remote branches (the work itself, pushed as it proceeds, including the id-keyed criteria artifact). Re-entering a half-done scope is therefore the SAME operation as starting it: the walker's ready-set arithmetic reads reality (Done → skipped; open PR → delivered-in-review per <issue id="d180640c-5311-4db5-945c-a3168fb3f951" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-58/approved-fire-auto-dispatch-the-tracker-side-producer-feeding-the-fire">KOD-58</issue> clause 5; crashed → eligible again), and a re-dispatched lane resumes ON its recorded branch, where the evaluator's first iteration grades existing state and only failing criteria drive new work. Death anywhere — rate limit, crash, restart — loses at most the in-flight iteration; tokens are spent only on the delta between durable reality and the scope's done-state. Hard rule this depends on: **branch-association lookup precedes branch minting on re-dispatch** — a re-fire must never mint a fresh uuid-suffixed branch and orphan remote partial work. **Amended by the 2026-08-07 execution run, twice.** (i) The rule generalizes: lookup-before-mint is one instance of a keyed write, and "re-entry is the same operation as starting" holds only if *every* tracker write is keyed. (ii) The rule is worth exactly what was recorded — a lane with commits on the remote and nothing in the tracker is the orphaning this rule forbids, reached from the other direction — so the association is not an identity written once, but a live record refreshed at commit cadence. Both are ruled in the section below.
* **Scope trigger meta-labels (founder, 2026-08-07).** The granular `queue:` vocabulary remains exactly as it is — per-issue eligibility within a scope. The v0.3 fire runner adds a **meta-label layer** one level up: the meta label set on an issue registers that issue **and its entire sub-issue subtree** as a standing scope; on a project, all its milestones and issues; on an initiative, everything under it. The meta label is the scope-level analog of the per-issue approval act — set by the approver role, recognized via state-change provenance (the <issue id="d180640c-5311-4db5-945c-a3168fb3f951" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-58/approved-fire-auto-dispatch-the-tracker-side-producer-feeding-the-fire">KOD-58</issue> discipline), resolved through OperationConfig's label mapping (exact label names are configuration, never literals in code). Two entry points, one resolution: an API-supplied ScopeRef and a tracker meta-label both resolve to the same scope run — the label is the tracker-native producer. The two label layers compose: the meta label admits the scope; the granular queue labels plus blockedBy arithmetic govern what fires inside it.
* **The approval label — the hierarchical human act (founder, 2026-08-07; name settled 2026-08-08; the vocabulary's keystone).** The meta-label family's key member: the approval label, set by the APPROVER (state-change provenance, the <issue id="d180640c-5311-4db5-945c-a3168fb3f951" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-58/approved-fire-auto-dispatch-the-tracker-side-producer-feeding-the-fire">KOD-58</issue> discipline) on any node of the hierarchy — initiative, project, milestone, issue — **approves implementation of everything within that node.** Resolution is an ancestor walk, computed never judged: an issue is execution-approved iff it or any ancestor (parent-issue chain → milestone → project → initiative) carries the approval label with approver provenance. One act at the top replaces N per-issue approval acts; `queue:approved` keeps its per-issue semantics for the standalone flow — inside an approved hierarchy, approval is inherited. **The label, concretely:** `scope:approved` — the name is settled (founder, 2026-08-08), and the literal stays one OperationConfig mapping entry, remappable without code, with code referencing the semantic member and never the string. **It is its own top-layer label, NOT a member of the** `queue:` **ladder, and there is deliberately no per-issue scope stamp:** approval is resolved by the ancestor walk at read time and never materialized onto the issues it covers, so nothing on an issue records that it sits inside an approved scope. The `queue:` ladder is untouched by the approval act and extends in place only by machine-set stage markers — `queue:triage` → `queue:proposed` → `queue:approved` (per-issue, standalone flow, unchanged), joined inside an approved scope by the machine-set stage sub-states of the staged-progression ruling below and closing at `queue:done`. So the [KOD-50](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-50/adopt-the-scheduled-routine-prompts-fire-prep-grooming-as-the>) enum gains the stage markers, the approval label sits in its own mapping entry beside `queue_states`, and there is no second state machine. The resolution arithmetic, the mapping entries and the adapter's carriage of the label are [KOD-73](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-73/v03-l1-scope-input-scoperef-tracker-port-container-vocabulary>) D5's and are not restated here. **Neither this charter nor any run creates the label or applies it.** Recording its name is not minting it, and applying it authorizes a fire — an act that belongs to the approver alone, which is what the approver-provenance requirement above exists to make checkable; the port-side refusal that turns a run's attempt into a failure rather than a discouragement is named on the lane whose sessions write to the tracker ([KOD-105](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-105/v03-l9-tracker-native-fire-composition-one-node-set-two-compositions>) D6). **Gating (corrected same day): the approval label gates the ENTIRE scope workflow — stages 1, 2, and 3. Without it the orchestrator does not touch the scope at all: no organizing, no criteria, no execution.** The cascade is re-checked per dispatch — handling revocation (removing the label stops the run at the next tick) and dynamic additions (a remediation follow-up parented inside the approved subtree resolves approved automatically — no human re-approval per remediation, deliberately). Fire prep is NOT part of the workflow: it keeps its own independent mandate — grooming and speccing not-yet-approved material — so an approval lands on well-prepped issues; it runs no stages and sets no stage labels. Adapter note: Linear natively carries labels on issues, projects, and initiatives; milestone-level carriage is an L1 adapter consult question (candidate: approve the project, scope the ScopeRef to the milestone). Open for consult: per-issue exclusion from an approved hierarchy; treatment of in-flight lanes on revocation.
* **The audit pass (grooming transformed — founder, 2026-08-07).** Grooming's v0.3 job is to double-check what the initiatives have been doing: an independent, fresh-context audit of the reconciler's claims — accepted tasks, cross-offs, evidence comments — re-verified against ground truth that cannot argue back (the anchors principle applied to the machine's own green lights). Verdicts are refutation-grounded; discrepancies are flagged or reopened with evidence, never silently corrected. Own lane: L7.
* **Staged progression with set-level barriers (founder, 2026-08-07).** Within an admitted scope the granular labels remain the run's state machine, extended with a stage family (ticket stage, criteria stage — names via OperationConfig): stage 1 drives every issue from its pre-state (stub / triage / proposed) to the ticket stage; stage 2 to the criteria stage; **the run advances only when ALL issues under the meta scope carry the current stage's label** — the barrier predicate is label arithmetic, computed never judged. **Amended by the 2026-08-07 execution run:** the barrier predicate is unchanged, but the label's *accept condition* is now specified — a stage's completion marker is set on an issue only when that issue passes the stage's admission test (stage 1: the fresh-context dry-implementation test; stage 2: a clean <issue id="0f2121ea-dc02-45c6-895a-3f9ed503f1f9" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-66/kodezart-generate-criteria-infeasible-or-mutually-unsatisfiable">KOD-66</issue> verdict, `unverifiable`-pending-blocker included). What changed: the barrier used to range over labels any pass could set, and now ranges over labels only an admission test can set. Breadth-first by stage is the coherence mechanism (criteria written with knowledge of all sibling specs), exactly as the 2026-08-07 manual sweep worked. **Stage labels are machine-set completion markers, not approval acts** — the human approval happened once, at scope admission via the meta label, and carries authority for the whole subtree; `queue:approved` keeps its per-issue human-act semantics for the standalone flow. Consequences: the walker dispatches **execution-only fires** (generation nodes bypassed for staged issues; each fire enters at the fire-time ruling node and then the ralph loop, with pre-validated criteria — **corrected by the 2026-08-07 execution run: "execution-only" means generation is never re-paid, never that a fire's inputs are decision-complete**), and stacked lanes get a cheap per-dispatch criteria re-validation against the resolved base through the <issue id="0f2121ea-dc02-45c6-895a-3f9ed503f1f9" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-66/kodezart-generate-criteria-infeasible-or-mutually-unsatisfiable">KOD-66</issue> gate (consult detail).
* **Fire prep as independent pre-warmer (founder, 2026-08-07; corrected same day).** Fire prep keeps its own independent mandate — grooming and speccing not-yet-approved material on its own cadence — so that when `scope:approved` lands, stage 1 finds well-prepped issues and moves fast (verify + label rather than author + label). Prep runs no workflow stages and sets no stage labels; the stage ladder is exclusively the approved run's ledger. One stage-writer (the run), with prep improving content upstream of it.

## Rulings from the execution run (the reference scope, run by hand — 2026-08-07/08)

**The recursion, stated plainly, because it is this charter's own thesis one turn further on.** The manual spec sweep of the v0.2 board is already recorded above as the behavioral spec for the organize step. The execution run that continued it — the same board, taken by hand from staged tickets to branches, commits and open PRs — is now the behavioral spec for the walker, the write-back and the audit. Its manual interventions were not incidents: each is a capability the machine would have had to exercise on the fly, and each is therefore recorded here as a ruling of this initiative rather than as an anecdote. Where a finding sharpens a ruling that already exists, that ruling is amended in place above and says what changed; only what is new is stated here. The evidence lives on the reference board — the run's own comments on the v0.2 lane fires — and is pointed at, never copied. The run's own account of itself is this initiative's document [Manual scope run, 2026-08-07/08 — behavioral spec for the walker, write-back and audit](<https://linear.app/duckburg/document/manual-scope-run-2026-08-0708-behavioral-spec-for-the-walker-write-b0732a8c090b>); read it there.

* **The tracker carries live run state at commit cadence, and the record is the re-entry index (founder-directed; execution run, 2026-08-07).** Recording the issue↔branch association *at dispatch* is already ruled and already specified on the owning lanes ([KOD-75](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-75/v03-l3-topology-planner-scope-walker-blockedby-graph-execution>) D2, consuming [KOD-67](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-67/issuebranch-mapping-so-stacked-work-composes-instead-of-colliding>)'s mapping) — that is not the delta; the run simply did not comply, and complying would still not have been enough. The delta is the record itself. Ruled: **each lane carries a live run-state record on the tracker, written by the same node that makes the commit and refreshed at commit cadence** — branch, head sha, commits ahead of base, push status, one row per commit with the issue it carries, diff size, and PR state once one exists. The writer that creates the state is the writer that records it: no polling loop, no side channel, no second process that can drift from reality. **Storage is ruled tracker-side**, closing a question [KOD-67](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-67/issuebranch-mapping-so-stacked-work-composes-instead-of-colliding>) deliberately left open (tracker-side vs. service-side), because the record's whole purpose is to be readable by a human and by a fresh agent with no access to the dead process's state — recorded as a forward supersession on the v0.3 side, the same pattern used for [KOD-51](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-51/pr-1-adapter-reliability-no-ci-classification-transient-404-tolerance>)'s node placement; no frozen v0.2 body is edited. The record is **marker-keyed and edited in place, never appended**, so a long lane leaves one always-current record instead of a stream of stale ones — the keyed-write ruling below applied to the system's highest-frequency write. **The notification split is a design decision, not a detail:** editing a record is silent in the tracker and posting one notifies, so the live record is EDITED (silent, always current) while lane EVENTS are POSTED — first push, PR opened, gate green, gate red, lane accepted, lane plateaued, issue crossed off. Progress a human has to poll for is progress learned too late; a notification per commit is noise; the split is what makes both true at once. And the record **says in its own text that it is the re-entry index**: the branch exists on the remote, check it out, never mint a new one, grade the existing commits against each sub-issue's Verification section, and let only failing criteria drive new work. *Evidence:* mid-run, lanes had commits pushed to the remote while the tracker said nothing about their branches at all — the association was scheduled for land time and those lanes had not reached land. A death at that moment leaves a human hunting branches on the forge and a restarting agent with nothing to look up: the orphaning the resumability ruling forbids, arrived at from the other direction. The repair was written by hand onto the reference board's live lane fires — a branch-link attachment plus a marker-keyed run-state comment carrying exactly those fields. **Those comments are the behavioral spec; build to them**, exactly as the manual sweep is the spec for organize. Lane: [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>).
* **A stage label needs an admission test, not a pass-through (execution run, 2026-08-07).** The barrier predicate stays label arithmetic; what was missing is the label's accept condition, now ruled and amended into the staged-progression ruling above. A barrier over unverified labels is a barrier that passes a scope which cannot execute, and the cost does not vanish — it lands in stage 3 as burned iteration budget. *Evidence:* the scope was declared staged, tickets and criteria present, and a fresh-context refutation pass asking exactly one question per issue — *could an implementer build this from the issue alone, without inventing a decision?* — found that nearly the whole board failed it, including every deliverable on the lanes that were about to fire. The failures were structural rather than stylistic: a criterion admitting two readings, one of which leaves the poll loop non-terminating; a criterion requiring the implementer to invent a response model and a probe call site; a body contradicting its own committed design. The test, its three-state verdict and its fail route are [KOD-74](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-74/v03-l2-organize-node-the-spec-pass-as-a-graph-step-make-everything-in>)'s.
* **A dispatched fire rules before it executes (execution run, 2026-08-07).** "Execution-only" means generation is never re-paid; it does not mean a fire may assume its inputs are decision-complete. Ambiguities surface only when an implementer actually tries, so a dispatched fire runs a **fire-time ruling node between dispatch and the ralph loop**: it rules each open question, writes the ruling to the tracker, and only then does the loop start — a ruling that exists only in a workflow's output did not happen. This is a different gate from the per-dispatch [KOD-66](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-66/kodezart-generate-criteria-infeasible-or-mutually-unsatisfiable>) re-validation and runs after it: that one grades criteria feasibility against a moved base, which is blind to spec ambiguity. The NEW-graph diagram drew the fire as starting at the ralph loop; the diagram and the staged-progression ruling are both corrected above. *Evidence:* the step was not empty on any lane that ran it — it pinned a response model, placed a lazy probe, fixed sleep ordering, defined the poll budget, and ruled the counter interaction that decides whether the poll loop terminates at all, and it re-grounded an issue whose stated defect is unreachable at the current base. Lane: [KOD-75](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-75/v03-l3-topology-planner-scope-walker-blockedby-graph-execution>).
* **One writer per surface, declared and enforced for the duration of a run (execution run, 2026-08-07).** [KOD-58](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-58/approved-fire-auto-dispatch-the-tracker-side-producer-feeding-the-fire>)'s dispatch answers *who may FIRE a lane* — under the founder's 2026-09-09 ruling, by the mark a worked lane carries and the walker skips on; nothing on the board answered *who may WRITE a surface*, and those are different exclusions — only one of them exists today. Ruled: every writable surface — issue description, marker-keyed comment, container description, container status update, label set — is **leased exclusively through the tracker port for the duration of a run**; a write to a surface the caller does not hold is a typed error, not a warning and not last-write-wins. Every writing component declares its surface set up front, and two components' declared sets must not intersect while both hold. Lane concurrency is safe precisely because lane surface sets are disjoint by construction; the surfaces that are *not* disjoint are the shared scope containers, which are ruled single-writer with the terminal as that writer. *Evidence:* the walker dispatches lanes concurrently and every fire writes to the tracker. In this run, separate repair passes each fixed the surface they owned and each falsified a statement on a surface they did not — one told a reader that dependency edges were still missing from the graph, edges the same workflow had recorded minutes earlier. A hand-maintained do-not-touch list was the only mutex the run had, and its absence is reliably fatal rather than occasionally untidy. Lane: [KOD-73](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-73/v03-l1-scope-input-scoperef-tracker-port-container-vocabulary>), as port surface beside the container reads.
* **No derived aggregate on a durable surface (execution run, 2026-08-07).** Ruled, and binding on every writing lane: a **durable** surface — an issue or container description, a marker-keyed live record, anything a reader reads as current — states stable facts only; counts, rosters, membership and any aggregate the tracker itself computes are queries, and embedding one manufactures a second source of truth that disagrees with the first. A **point-in-time** surface — a status update, a terminal report, an event payload — may carry aggregates, because it is timestamped and never read as current. That distinction, not "computed rather than judged", is what makes the terminal's progress report a status update instead of a description edit. *Evidence:* a repair pass wrote an issue count into summarizing surfaces and then created issues, falsifying its own text within the hour; a later pass reproduced the class on a different surface. The rule already governs this body and the v0.2 board's, so it must equally govern what the machine writes — which means an enforcement point on the outbound write path rather than a convention. Lane: [KOD-78](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-78/v03-l6-scope-terminal-per-lane-outcome-vector-initiative-progress>).
* **Idempotency generalizes past branches (execution run, 2026-08-07).** The charter already rules that branch-association lookup precedes branch minting; ruled now, and amended into the resumability ruling above: the same rule binds **every** tracker write — marker-keyed comments edited in place, assert-then-edit descriptions, check-before-create PRs, issue creation keyed by deliverable identity, set-if-different labels and states. The property to hold is single: running a writing component twice over the same input leaves the tracker as it was after running it once, and creates no second object. *Evidence:* as things stand, a cold re-run of this run's scaffolding step would mint a second set of issues rather than recognize the first. Lane: [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>).
* **Audit runs at two cadences, and they are not the same mechanism (execution run, 2026-08-07).** L7 is the standing independent audit over recorded Done claims — re-verified against the branch that carries each, per Ruling A — and it does **not** discharge the inline obligation: each writing pass verifies its own output in fresh context, under the same information conditions, before the next consumer reads it. Nor does inline verification remove the need for an independent second reader — the verifier of a pass can itself introduce a defect, which is exactly why inline verification is a round in a convergence loop while L7 is the independent reader of what converged. *Evidence:* every fresh-context verification pass in this run found something, including defects created by the pass it was verifying. That is write-write skew, and a standing audit is far too slow to catch it before the bad output is consumed. The non-substitution is stated on [KOD-79](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-79/v03-l7-audit-pass-grooming-transformed-critically-evaluate-the>); the inline obligation is named on each writing lane that lacks it.
* **Convergence is a loop, not a pass (execution run, 2026-08-07).** A repair or organize pass is scoped to a defect **class**, never to an enumerated findings list, and repeats until a fresh-context verification round over **every surface the pass may write** — not merely the surfaces it did write — returns no finding of that class. Rounds are bounded by configuration; exhausting the bound halts with the surviving findings as a first-class outcome, never a silent advance. "The pass made no writes" and the heartbeat's delta pre-query are cost gates over tracker state: neither can see a spec-quality defect, so neither is the stopping condition. *Evidence:* bringing one layer of the board to consistency took repeated passes with diminishing findings, and each pass scoped to a findings list reproduced its own defect class on surfaces the list did not name — the measured failure mode is a pass fixing one surface and breaking another. Lane: [KOD-74](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-74/v03-l2-organize-node-the-spec-pass-as-a-graph-step-make-everything-in>).
* **Surfaces have a declared precedence, so disagreement is resolved by arithmetic (execution run, 2026-08-07/08).** Two surfaces on a live board will eventually disagree; what a machine cannot do is choose between them without a rule, and this run had none, so every contradiction cost a human ruling. Ruled: one precedence order, applied without judgment, in three tiers — **the relation graph beats an issue body; an issue body beats a summarizing surface; and the document that OWNS a rule beats any restatement of it, wherever that restatement sits.** The graph tier is the tracker's own structure — edges, parentage, container membership — which is what "the graph is the machine" already means one level up. The ownership tier is the operative one for rules rather than facts: it makes a restatement a defect to delete rather than a claim to weigh, and it is why this body's Progress line points at the v0.2 protocol instead of carrying a copy of it. Precedence is the read-side counterpart of the write-side leases ruled above and specified on [KOD-73](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-73/v03-l1-scope-input-scoperef-tracker-port-container-vocabulary>): a lease decides who may write a surface; precedence decides what a reader believes once two of them have already been written. *Evidence:* a milestone stated one intra-lane order while its own fire had ruled a different one, and the project and the initiative carried two different versions of the central crossing gate, under one of which a milestone was permanently uncrossable. Each cost a human to say which surface won. Declared once, *which do I believe* becomes computed; undeclared, every disagreement either stops the machine or — worse — does not. Binds every component that reads or writes the tracker; no single lane owns it.
* **A writer reports what its own edits falsified (execution run, 2026-08-07/08).** Ruled as a REQUIRED output of every write-back rather than a habit of careful writers: a component that finishes writing names the statements its edits have just made false on surfaces it does not hold, and reports them to those surfaces' holders — never repairing them itself, since writing a surface it does not hold is exactly what the lease ruling above forbids. It is the cheapest check available: the writer still holds the context needed to answer, where any later reader has to reconstruct it, and requiring the answer changes what the writer re-reads before it finishes. This is a third obligation, distinct from the two audit cadences above and from the non-substitution invariant stated on [KOD-79](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-79/v03-l7-audit-pass-grooming-transformed-critically-evaluate-the>) — those govern verifying the artifact a pass *did* produce, and neither looks at the blast radius of an edit on a neighbouring surface. *Evidence:* every repair pass in this run left at least one neighbouring statement false, and not one noticed unaided; each was found afterwards by a fresh-context reader, by which time the false statement had been available to be read as input. Binds every writing component, on every lane.
* **Hunt the instruction, not only the copies (execution run, 2026-08-08).** A node that removes instances of a defect while leaving in place the text that mandates them has not converged — it has scheduled the recurrence, and the next pass regrows exactly what this one deleted. So the done-condition of any node that removes a defect class from the tracker includes that no surface still instructs writers to produce it. *Evidence:* the duplicated central crossing gate on the reference board was not accidental copying — a milestone-facing surface's own text told writers to duplicate it ("each milestone description states this condition explicitly and names its fire"), so every copy was compliance with a live instruction, and deleting the copies alone would have left the instruction running. The done-conditions belong to the nodes that remove defects: [KOD-74](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-74/v03-l2-organize-node-the-spec-pass-as-a-graph-step-make-everything-in>) (organize and its repair rounds) and [KOD-79](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-79/v03-l7-audit-pass-grooming-transformed-critically-evaluate-the>) (the audit).
* **A terminal declares its stopping point and hands over the residual (execution run, 2026-08-08).** A convergence loop needs a legible end, so a scope run's terminal must be able to say which of three things happened — converged; converged with a declared residual; stopped short — with the residual carried as data rather than narrated. An unconverged run is a legible outcome, never a silent truncation and never an open-ended grind. *Evidence:* in this run the stopping rule was declared aloud before the final repair pass — if this does not converge I stop and hand over the residual rather than run another pass — and that declaration is what made a partial result usable to the next reader instead of unbounded. Lane: [KOD-78](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-78/v03-l6-scope-terminal-per-lane-outcome-vector-initiative-progress>), which owns the outcome vocabulary and the residual's shape; a stage-level halt carrying its surviving findings is [KOD-74](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-74/v03-l2-organize-node-the-spec-pass-as-a-graph-step-make-everything-in>)'s.
* **An escalation is written when it is raised, never carried to the terminal (execution run, 2026-08-08).** A node that raises a question the run cannot answer writes it to the tracker in the same act as raising it — on the owning issue, with the decision label and the pinned interim reading — never returned as data for a later stage to surface. The terminal aggregates and reports; it must never be the first writer of anything. This is the write-when-known rule the live-run-state ruling above applies to associations, generalized to every class of thing a run learns that someone else must act on: associations, rulings, amendments, escalations, criteria verdicts. *Evidence:* a session limit killed this run's agents mid-flight; every commit survived, and every fire-time ruling survived because rulings were written to the tracker in the same act as making them — while the escalations those same nodes raised did not survive, having been returned as data for a land stage to surface, every land stage having died, and they were recovered only because a human read a dead process's output buffer, which is not a mechanism. The full account is the F16 comment on [KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>); the write site sits with [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>)/[KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>), the raising node is [KOD-94](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-94/fire-time-ruling-node-rule-every-open-question-onto-the-tracker-before>), and [KOD-78](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-78/v03-l6-scope-terminal-per-lane-outcome-vector-initiative-progress>) is the surface this rule forbids from being anyone's first writer.

## The supervision graph — what it replaces, and what it never will

Founder requirement, verbatim: *"I need a graph to replace my personal supervision in the new model."* This section names what that supervision consists of, because a job that is never named is never delegated — it is merely left undone and noticed late. The evidence is the execution run recorded above: the list below is not a taxonomy of oversight in general, it is what one human actually had to do over one run of one board, and each entry is therefore a capability the graph must have rather than a virtue it should aspire to.

**What supervision actually did, and what answers for it now.**

| the supervisory act, as observed | what answers for it |
| -- | -- |
| Noticed a lane reading zero satisfied criteria while its gate was green, and asked why | Nothing. Both readings exist and nothing compares them against each other. Job two below |
| Ruled a definitional question the run could not settle — what Done means | Irreducibly human (Ruling A) |
| Corrected a scope boundary the run had assumed — that it may merge | Irreducibly human (Ruling B) |

Two of its rules are load-bearing for this charter and neither is currently reachable by the lane that would enforce it. **The workspace rule:** the supervisor keeps no private scratch surface — findings become issues and comments as they are formed, because anything held for a summary dies with the pass, and the pass is the thing that dies. **The conduct rules:** four of the eleven supervise the *runner's* conduct and output quality rather than the *work's* state — that a node was run as one session rather than decomposed, that a prediction preceded an observation, that an aggregate was re-derived rather than restated, that a finding changes what gets built rather than restating this charter. "Computed, never judged" does not reach any of them. Whether that boundary moves, or whether a second mechanism sits beside it, is `KOD-79` and `KOD-103`'s question to rule and not this charter's to assume.

**Two jobs, and only one of them is built.**

**Job one — holding intent against output.** Does what the run produced match what was asked of it? This is a reader comparing an artifact against a stated intent, and it is largely covered: the criterion amendment reconciler ([KOD-97](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-97/criterion-amendment-reconciler-default-upheld-amend-only-on-a-self>)) holds a criterion against a run that wants it changed, the audit ([KOD-79](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-79/v03-l7-audit-pass-grooming-transformed-critically-evaluate-the>)) holds a Done claim against the branch that supposedly carries it, the organize admission test ([KOD-74](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-74/v03-l2-organize-node-the-spec-pass-as-a-graph-step-make-everything-in>)) holds a spec against whether anyone could build from it, and the falsification obligation above holds a writer's edits against the surfaces it does not hold.

**Job two — watching the run's own shape.** Is this run behaving like a run that is working? Nothing covers it. These findings are distinguished by being visible *without reading the work at all*: a tally that does not move, a stage that reports without having advanced, a cadence that stops, a ratio that cannot be true. No reconciler can raise them, because a reconciler compares one lane's artifact against one lane's intent and each of those comparisons can pass while the run as a whole is plainly malfunctioning — the observed case being a green gate over a zero tally, where both readings were internally consistent and their conjunction was not. **The job is assigned to its own lane in this initiative's project — named here, specified there.** This section deliberately states no threshold, no alarm condition and no cadence; the vocabulary that lets an alarm exist on the tracker at all is in the port-widening section below, and it is carriage only.

**What stays human even with the whole graph built.** Three acts, and naming them is the point of this section rather than a caveat on it — a supervisor who cannot say which of their acts is irreducible has to keep performing all of them, so this list is what makes everything above delegable.

* **Definitional rulings.** What Done means (Ruling A). Not because a machine cannot state a definition, but because the definition is the standard its own output is graded against: a run permitted to settle it would be choosing the test it is about to sit.
* **Scope boundaries.** That the machine opens pull requests and never merges them (Ruling B). A boundary the run may move is not a boundary; its whole content is that it is not the run's to revise.
* **Approval itself.** The one human act at every tick, already ruled as the gate on the entire workflow, and unchanged by anything here.

**Irreducible does not mean blocking, and the difference is a mechanism.** A run that meets one of these does not stop and wait: it writes the question to the tracker in the same act as raising it, pins the interim reading it will proceed under, and continues — the human ruling then either confirms the interim reading or refutes it, which is the same shape as an audit refutation and re-enters through the same path as any other criterion that lands in the gap. Where no interim reading may be assumed, the lane halts with that stated as its outcome rather than grinding. The graph's obligation towards an irreducibly human act is therefore not to decide it but to **ask legibly and on time** — which is exactly the failure the run exhibited, having raised its escalations and then lost them.

## The gap is the unit of work (design ruling, 2026-08-08)

**Ruled.** A pass over an approved scope does not carry a lane, a stage, or a task list. It carries a **gap** — the difference between where the scope's acceptance criteria currently stand and completion — computed at entry from durable state, and **closed** rather than redone.

The gap's members are **obligations** — never lanes. *Corrected 2026-08-08:* this line read "criteria, together with a lane's own checks", which is one kind short of the arithmetic its own lane specifies. `KOD-75` D10a rules three kinds — a criterion, a **pinned ruling's compliance**, and a lane check — and argues the omission directly: a gap ranging over too few kinds reads empty on a lane that is not Done, and the walk then halts with work outstanding, which is the deadlock the Done arithmetic exists to prevent. The membership case named below as "satisfied but resting on a violation" is ruling-compliance expressed as a property of a criterion; that is not equivalent, because a violated ruling with no criterion attached is invisible under it.

**A lane closes when its gap empties, never when a fire ends (founder, 2026-08-08).** The consequence of the ruling above, stated because it is the one an implementer inverts. Every issue is on the tracker, so a pass carries the gap and closes it; a tick is not required to finish a lane, only to shrink it. **Lane size is therefore not a terminal condition** — a one-issue lane and a twelve-issue lane differ only in tick count, and no tick needs to know how many preceded it.

The wiring that would break this is a single line: map a fire's terminal outcome — budget exhausted, not accepted, plateaued — onto the lane, and every lane larger than one fire's iteration budget stops permanently, reported as failed while its gap is non-empty and shrinking. A fire's outcome is the result of **one dispatch**; the per-fire iteration budget is a per-tick bound, not a per-lane one. A lane is dispatchable while its gap is non-empty and for no other reason, and there are exactly three terminals: converged, halted on the barren-tick bound, or converged with a declared residual. "Too large" is not among them, and no estimate of whether a lane *can* finish may be an input to dispatch — that is judgment, in the one component whose whole discipline is that it computes and never judges. `KOD-116` owns the deliverable and its fixtures.

Filed rather than assumed because the 2026-08-08 dry run's own supervisor, holding the full board and every ruling, predicted in writing that one lane "is not closable in a few ticks" and framed it as something to plan around. A reader with complete context defaulted to a size-based stop; an implementer wiring the outcome enum will too, and the resulting defect is invisible, because the lane simply stops being dispatched. A criterion is in the gap when it is not a satisfied grading at the head that carries the work: failing, never graded, lapsed because the head moved, satisfied but resting on a violation, or newly arrived by amendment. The arithmetic that decides membership and the records it reads belong to [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>) and [KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>); turning a per-criterion gap into dispatchable lanes is [KOD-75](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-75/v03-l3-topology-planner-scope-walker-blockedby-graph-execution>)'s ready-set arithmetic; the spec-defect analog one stage up is [KOD-74](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-74/v03-l2-organize-node-the-spec-pass-as-a-graph-step-make-everything-in>)'s convergence loop. None of it is restated here.

**The unification, which is why this is a ruling and not a definition.** The charter above treats three situations separately. Under this ruling they are one operation, differing only in what put criteria into the gap:

* **re-entry after a crash** — criteria are in the gap because nothing graded them at the current head;
* **re-entry after an audit refutation** — criteria are in the gap because an independent reader moved them there with evidence ([KOD-79](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-79/v03-l7-audit-pass-grooming-transformed-critically-evaluate-the>));
* **a heartbeat tick over a standing scope** — criteria are in the gap because the scope acquired them, because an amendment added them ([KOD-97](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-97/criterion-amendment-reconciler-default-upheld-amend-only-on-a-self>)), or because a base moved beneath them.

One path, three producers. A machine that distinguishes the three needs three recovery mechanisms, will have exercised one of them, and will discover the other two in the incident that needed them.

**What the ruling forbids, so it is checkable rather than aspirational.**

* **No pass re-does what is already satisfied at head.** Re-running generation, minting a second branch for an issue that has one, or resetting an issue wholesale destroys the very record the gap is computed from — the prohibition on wholesale reset already sits with the state arithmetic, and this is its reason.
* **The gap is computed, never remembered.** It is derived at entry from tracker state plus the remote branch, and never carried in process state or read from a plan a previous pass wrote down. A remembered gap is a second source of truth about the first, and it is wrong the moment anything else writes.
* **An empty gap is an outcome, not a no-op.** It is the fixpoint: the scope is converged, and the tick says so.

This ruling names the thing that the resumability ruling and the heartbeat section both call *the delta*. Neither is restated here; both now have one referent, and the cost consequence stated in the heartbeat section is a consequence of this definition rather than a separate claim.

## The tracker port widens — a forward supersession, not a Linear feature

**The system is not Linear.** It is a vendor-neutral tracker port with a conformance suite, owned by [KOD-57](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-57/vendor-neutral-tracker-port-linear-adapter-first-of-n-github-issues>); Linear is its first adapter, and GitHub Issues or Jira are alternative adapters behind the same port rather than rewrites. v0.3 needs that port to carry more than its v0.2 surface does, and **every addition is recorded exactly the way the container vocabulary already is: a forward supersession — the v0.2 port ships narrow as specced, v0.3 widens it as its own conformance-tested surface, and no frozen v0.2 body is edited.** [KOD-57](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-57/vendor-neutral-tracker-port-linear-adapter-first-of-n-github-issues>) stays the owner of the narrow version and of the suite by which the widened surface is tested.

**Every capability is stated in three layers, in this order.** A writer who begins at the third has designed a Linear feature and will discover it when a second adapter is attempted.

1. **Domain vocabulary on the port.** What the thing is, in the language of the domain. *The satisfaction state of a criterion, and the commit it was graded at* is domain vocabulary. *A ticked checkbox in a description* is one vendor's rendering of it.
2. **A conformance property.** The port's guarantee, stated so that any adapter can be held to it and the conformance suite can execute it. The essential shape is round-trip fidelity: **write a domain value through the port, read it back through the port, get the same domain value.** Stated at the port, it binds every future adapter; stated at the adapter, it binds only today's.
3. **Adapter mapping, labelled as such.** How one adapter satisfies the property with whatever that vendor happens to offer. Implementation detail of one adapter, and no consumer may know any of it.

**What v0.3 adds to the port.** Each entry is vocabulary plus the property an adapter is held to; the owning lane specifies it and contributes its cases to the suite.

* **Criterion satisfaction, stamped with the commit it was graded at.** Per-criterion, addressed by criterion identity. *Property:* a set of per-criterion satisfaction values written for an issue reads back as the same set, with identity, state and graded sha preserved, addressed by identity and never by position and never by matching the criterion's text. Lanes: [KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>), [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>).
* **Work-ref association — one issue, several refs, distinct roles.** Two-level branching is live and is not deprecated: a feature ref, the iteration ref the loop works on, recovery refs, and the best-iteration ref a do-not-merge stall PR is opened from, which exists nowhere else. All three shapes are on origin at `main` @ `92597c0`; `git ls-remote --heads origin` is the check. *Property:* associations written for one issue under distinct roles all read back, roles preserved and distinguishable, and re-writing a role updates that association rather than adding a second. A port that holds one ref per issue cannot express a stall exit, which is why this is vocabulary and not a convenience. Lanes: [KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>), consuming [KOD-67](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-67/issuebranch-mapping-so-stacked-work-composes-instead-of-colliding>)'s mapping.
* **The live run-state record.** *Property:* written through the port and read back verbatim, and keyed — writing twice under one key leaves one current record rather than a stream of stale ones. Lane: [KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>).
* **An open decision — an escalation carrying an interim reading, which ages.** *Property:* it reads back with its interim reading intact and with the moment it was raised, so its age is computed by the reader and never stored as a number on the record (the no-derived-aggregate rule); and open decisions are **enumerable across a scope** without knowing in advance which issues hold them, since an escalation nobody can find is the failure this vocabulary exists to prevent. Raised by [KOD-94](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-94/fire-time-ruling-node-rule-every-open-question-onto-the-tracker-before>); write site with [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>)/[KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>).
* **A run-shape alarm.** A machine-raised statement that the run's own shape is implausible. It names no decision, which is what distinguishes it from an open decision, and it persists until cleared, which is what distinguishes it from an event. *Property:* keyed, so a condition that holds for an hour is one alarm and not a stream; readable as raised or cleared, with the sha at each. What raises one, on what threshold, at what cadence, belongs to the lane named in the supervision section and appears nowhere here — this is carriage.
* **Per-criterion evidence.** *Property:* evidence written against a criterion identity is retrievable by that identity, so a reader fetches the evidence for one criterion without reading a thread; and evidence **accumulates where satisfaction replaces** — a refutation attaches its evidence without destroying the evidence of the pass it overturns, because an audit that erases what it refutes leaves nothing for the next audit to weigh. Lanes: [KOD-76](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-76/v03-l4-tracker-as-live-run-state-evaluator-write-back-validation-from>), [KOD-79](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-79/v03-l7-audit-pass-grooming-transformed-critically-evaluate-the>).

Several of these will map onto one mechanism in any given adapter. That is an adapter fact and never a reason to collapse them at the port: their properties differ — a run-state record is always current, an open decision ages, evidence accumulates — and a port that merges them loses exactly those differences.

**Adapter mapping — Linear, one implementation of the above, and no part of the vocabulary.** Marker-keyed comments carry the keyed records; link attachments with role-bearing titles carry work-refs; a label carries the open-decision enumeration; a status update is the point-in-time surface aggregates are allowed to live on. **Every mapping is proven by writing the value and reading it back through an independent read rather than a write echo, and never asserted.** Proven for the keyed records on 2026-08-08 on this initiative: the probe record in this initiative's comments states which properties passed, and more usefully the one a write-and-read-back cannot observe. The role-bearing attachment mapping was proven separately by the lane that owns it and records its own evidence; this section claims no credit for it. The probe also records a hazard already visible on this board — a value damaged in authoring and never detected, because nothing read it back and compared, which is the argument for machine-read values being addressable records rather than text parsed out of prose.

**Capability is declared and checked at boot, never degraded at runtime.** Some vendors will not carry some shapes. Graceful degradation is forbidden, so the answer is not a fallback: **the port declares the capabilities it requires, an adapter declares what it provides, and a mismatch aborts startup with a typed error naming the missing capability and the port concept that needs it** — the fail-loud shape already used for OperationConfig's boot validation and the sanitization gate's fail-closed default. This is the mechanism by which [KOD-57](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-57/vendor-neutral-tracker-port-linear-adapter-first-of-n-github-issues>)'s standing rule — a backend that cannot express a required concept is a documented refusal, not a runtime surprise — actually refuses, and it does not weaken that rule: the declarations are compared once, at boot, and never read again, so no consumer branches on a capability and no feature detection exists at runtime. A run must never discover mid-flight that its tracker cannot record a cross-off. **The mechanism is not re-specified here:** the capability vocabulary beside the port and the boot validation that compares required against provided are specified on [KOD-96](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-96/live-lane-run-state-record-marker-keyed-edited-at-commit-cadence-and>), and each lane adds the member its own concept requires. What this section owns is which capabilities the widened port requires of any adapter, and why each is load-bearing.

The capabilities an adapter must declare, each with what fails loudly in its absence: **several independently addressable durable records per item** (without it there are no cross-offs, no run-state record, no evidence); **several role-tagged refs per item** (no stall exit, no two-level branching); **per-item state with transition provenance**, already required by the narrow port (no approval act, since authority binds to who performed the transition); **a queryable attribute for enumerating open decisions across a container** (escalations become unfindable and writing them at the moment they are raised buys nothing); **container membership reads** (no ScopeRef, per [KOD-73](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-73/v03-l1-scope-input-scoperef-tracker-port-container-vocabulary>)); **exclusive write leases** (concurrent lanes corrupt shared surfaces, per [KOD-73](<https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-73/v03-l1-scope-input-scoperef-tracker-port-container-vocabulary>)); **a point-in-time surface distinct from durable ones** (the terminal's aggregates have nowhere legal to go and the no-derived-aggregate rule becomes unsatisfiable); and **a silent-update surface distinct from a notifying one** (the edit-versus-post split collapses, and progress is either unnoticed or noise).

**Verification.** Each property above becomes a named case in the port-level conformance suite, contributed by the lane that owns the concept and run verbatim against every adapter over the in-process fake tracker in CI, with no live workspace: for each concept, a value written through the port and read back through the port compares equal; a value written twice under one key leaves one object; a role-tagged association set survives with its roles distinguishable; an open decision is found by enumeration over a container without being addressed directly; evidence written by a refuting pass leaves the refuted pass's evidence present. Boot cases: an adapter declaring a capability the port requires starts; an adapter missing one aborts with a typed error naming that capability and the concept requiring it; and no code path reads a capability declaration after boot.

## Dependencies

v0.3 consumes the v0.2 end-state. Which v0.2 organ a lane consumes, and why it cannot be built before that organ exists, is a fact about the lane: it is carried by that lane's own recorded relations and argued on the lane itself, where it can be checked against the artifact it names.

**No prerequisite is stated here, and none is to be added.** A dependency written at container level asserts a blanket claim over every member, which is strictly stronger than the truth — it cannot say that one lane consumes an organ while its neighbour consumes nothing from it, and the graph says exactly that. It is also uncheckable: an edge can be tested against the artifact it claims to carry; a sentence cannot. And an initiative-level prerequisite is not homeless for want of an edge type — the lane fires hold `blockedBy` edges, and edges crossing from the v0.2 board into this one are already in use — so pushing the fact down onto the members that hold it is the accurate expression rather than a workaround for a missing one.

A prerequisite phrased as *having landed* is unsatisfiable by anything in the loop besides, for the reason the Design rulings above give.

*Decomposed 2026-08-08. The container-level prerequisites this section carried were tested lane by lane against the artifact each names; where a lane consumes one, the edge is recorded on that lane with its reason beside it. Some lanes hold no such edge, because they consume nothing from the named work — the sentence asserted otherwise of every member and was wrong about part of its own scope.*

## Cron evolution: from workers to heartbeat (founder consult, 2026-08-07)

In v0.2 the scheduled passes are three time-driven **workers** — fire-prep (judgment), grooming (cleanup judgment), and the auto-dispatch scheduler pass (arithmetic) — each rebuilding context per tick, with conservative cadence because prep/groom ticks are full agent sessions. In v0.3 those three turn out to be fragments of the scope loop, and the cron's meaning inverts: it stops doing the work and becomes **the heartbeat of one reconciler** — "re-enter each standing scope at least every N" (a liveness floor / resync interval), not "do the work every N".

| v0.2 cron | v0.3 identity |
| -- | -- |
| Fire-prep pass | Splits: its classic mandate (groom/spec not-yet-approved material) continues as its own pass; organize re-entry belongs to the reconciler tick and runs only over APPROVED standing scopes |
| Auto-dispatch pass | The walker's ready-set tick (same eligibility arithmetic, scope-wide, with a marked lane skipped) |
| Grooming pass | **Transformed, not absorbed (founder correction 2026-08-07): grooming becomes the AUDIT pass (L7)** — an independent, fresh-context critical evaluation of what the scope runs claim: accepted tasks re-verified against ground truth (evidence comments vs actual tests/branches/PRs; accepted criteria re-checked against the branch carrying the work), discrepancies flagged or reopened with evidence, never silently trusted. The reconciler must never solely grade its own work at the operating level |

**Resumability is what makes the heartbeat affordable — the two rulings are one design.** A tick opens with the deterministic pre-query (<issue id="074f3e14-46b9-4f75-9d8a-5139ede45ad9" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-60/prep-grooming-pass-parity-and-routine-cutover-scheduled-passes-run">KOD-60</issue>'s cost gate; under <issue id="188b3e2c-8b7c-430e-8ec6-27d9a6cf3764" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-57/vendor-neutral-tracker-port-linear-adapter-first-of-n-github-issues">KOD-57</issue>'s mechanism ruling a zero-token port call), whose v0.3 meaning is "is there a delta?": no delta → nothing wakes, the tick costs a few API reads; delta → only the delta is paid (idempotent organize, delta-priced re-entry, evaluator-as-reconciler). Cadence can therefore tighten; the eventual accelerant is event-driven re-entry (tracker webhooks) with cron as the resync floor — deliberately a future step, not implied scope.

**Standing scopes:** the heartbeat re-enters registered standing scopes and converges each to its fixpoint — everything approved and unblocked delivered — then idles at empty-delta with a legible outcome (<issue id="d180640c-5311-4db5-945c-a3168fb3f951" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-58/approved-fire-auto-dispatch-the-tracker-side-producer-feeding-the-fire">KOD-58</issue>'s "approved-but-blocked is a correct resting state", generalized). Approval remains the only human act at every tick; a standing reconciler cannot run away because the walker dispatches only approved, unblocked lanes and skips a lane already carrying the in-progress mark.

**Two-stage cutover:** stage 1 (v0.2, <issue id="074f3e14-46b9-4f75-9d8a-5139ede45ad9" href="https://linear.app/duckburg/issue/KOD-60/prep-grooming-pass-parity-and-routine-cutover-scheduled-passes-run">KOD-60</issue>) moves the passes from the external scheduler into kodezart at behavior parity; stage 2 (v0.3) dissolves them into reconciler ticks. * **Per-PR checks never evaluate the union, so "CI folded in" is not the same as verified.** The concept map retires `monitor_ci` on the grounds that the landing machinery watches checks itself, and it does — per PR. A forge runs a pull request's checks against that PR's head merged with **its own base**, never against a sibling PR. Under Ruling B, several open PRs at once is the steady state, so the state a human eventually merges is evaluated by nothing, and a scope terminal can report every lane green over a union that does not build.
